guide.title: Allergy & Anaphylaxis
guide.lead: Anaphylaxis kills by swelling, wheeze or shock, often within minutes. The only first-line drug is IM epinephrine into the thigh, given early and repeated if needed. Antihistamines are not the treatment. Low BP is not needed to make the diagnosis.

sections.title: Is it anaphylaxis?
sections.question: After exposure (food, sting, drug), skin or mucosal signs plus any of these? Or one of these after a known allergen even without skin signs?
items: Breathing: wheeze, stridor, hoarse voice, breathlessness, low SpO₂
sections.no: Local or mild allergic reaction: monitor, antihistamine per protocol, reassess.

doses.dose: 0.15 mg (about 15–30 kg); 0.3 mg (30 kg or more)

steps.title: Position
steps.text: Lying with legs raised if BP is low; sitting if breathing is the problem; never stand up suddenly.

steps.title: Oxygen, call ALS, monitor
steps.text: Remove the trigger if still present (sting).

steps.title: Repeat
steps.text: Another IM dose after 5 minutes if not improving.

steps.title: Still not improving after 2 doses
steps.text: Refractory: IV epinephrine infusion and fluid bolus (500–1000 mL adult, 10 mL/kg child).

sections.title: After epinephrine
items: Antihistamines and steroids are second-line: they don't treat airway swelling, wheeze or shock
Biphasic reactions happen in up to 5%
Hospital observation: at least 6 hours, 12 hours after 2 doses or a severe reaction

quiz.q: Bee sting 10 minutes ago: hives, wheeze, BP 88/50. First drug?
options: IM epinephrine into the anterolateral thigh

quiz.q: Hives and mild wheeze after eating peanuts; BP 118/76, SpO₂ 95%. Anaphylaxis?
options: Yes: any peanut reaction is anaphylaxis

quiz.q: Ten minutes after epinephrine, wheeze returns and SpO₂ falls to 89%. Do:
quiz.explanation: Repeat after 5 minutes if not improving.
Of the 1 mg/mL solution, into the thigh.

options: Second-line, for itch and hives only
They replace epinephrine if BP is normal

quiz.q: Best position for a hypotensive anaphylaxis patient:
quiz.explanation: Sitting if breathing is the main problem; never stand suddenly.
So everyone is observed in hospital.

quiz.q: No improvement after 2 IM doses. This is:
options: Refractory anaphylaxis: IV epinephrine and fluids (ALS)

flashcards.question: Anaphylaxis definition
flashcards.answer: A severe systemic reaction: skin or mucosal signs plus breathing, circulation or severe gut problems; or breathing or circulation problems after a known allergen even without skin signs.

flashcards.question: Signs by system
flashcards.answer: Airway: tongue swelling, stridor, hoarse voice. Breathing: wheeze, low SpO₂. Circulation: low BP, collapse. Skin: hives, flushing, swelling. Gut: cramps, vomiting.

flashcards.question: First-line treatment
flashcards.answer: IM epinephrine into the anterolateral thigh: the only drug that reverses the whole reaction. Delay is linked to deaths.

flashcards.question: Epinephrine doses
flashcards.answer: 0.01 mg/kg IM of 1 mg/mL, maximum 0.5 mg (adult 0.5 mg). Auto-injectors 0.15 mg (about 15–30 kg) or 0.3 mg (30 kg or more).

flashcards.question: Repeating epinephrine
flashcards.answer: After 5 minutes if not improving. No improvement after 2 doses: refractory, IV epinephrine (ALS).

flashcards.question: Antihistamines
flashcards.answer: Second-line: help itch and hives, but don't treat airway swelling, bronchospasm or shock.

flashcards.question: Biphasic anaphylaxis
flashcards.answer: Symptoms return hours later in up to 5%. Observe in hospital at least 6 hours (12 hours after 2 doses or a severe reaction).

flashcards.question: Positioning
flashcards.answer: Lying with legs raised if hypotensive; sitting if breathing is the problem; never stand up suddenly.

critical.scenario: 15 minutes after eating shrimp, a 24-year-old has wheeze, hives, swollen lips and says her throat is closing. SpO₂ 91%, BP 104/68.
critical.question: Treatment sequence?

options.t: IM epinephrine 0.5 mg into the thigh now, oxygen, sit her up, call ALS, transport
Wait for low BP before epinephrine
Lie her flat with legs raised
options.f: Breathing is the problem: let her sit.

critical.explanation: Skin, airway and breathing involvement: anaphylaxis. Repeat after 5 minutes if not improving.

critical.scenario: A 7-year-old (20 kg) with known wasp allergy was stung: facial hives, wheeze, vomiting, SpO₂ 93%. His mother hands you his auto-injector.
critical.question: Dose and site?

options.t: 0.15 mg IM into the anterolateral thigh

options.f: Thigh, and 0.3 mg is for 30 kg or more.

critical.explanation: Weight-based: 0.01 mg/kg = 0.2 mg; the 0.15 mg device is the right auto-injector.

critical.scenario: 8 minutes after epinephrine, a patient who had improved says her throat is tight again; wheeze is back, SpO₂ 91%, BP down from 118/74 to 98/64. 12 minutes to hospital.
critical.question: Next action?

options.t: Repeat IM epinephrine in the other thigh, oxygen, monitor, notify the hospital

options.f: Repeat after 5 minutes if not improving.

options.t: Sit her bolt upright and stand her up to walk in
options.f: Never stand an anaphylaxis patient up suddenly.

critical.explanation: If 2 doses fail, it's refractory: ALS for IV epinephrine and fluids.
